description: Fully responsive interactive hanging mobile/scale puzzle tool where students categorize six puzzles by difficulty, then solve each by finding the unknown weight value. Built with the Singularity Design System (Poppins font, #4A4DC9/#FF7212 palette, #533086→#FC9145 gradients). Adapts from mobile (320px) to desktop (860px+) via ResizeObserver container queries.
topic: Finding Unknown Weights: Hanging Scale Problems (Fig 7.1 to 7.5)
subject: Mathematics
learningObjectives: Understand how hanging mobiles/scales balance when total weight is distributed
Find unknown weights using arithmetic reasoning (total minus known = unknown portion)
Categorize problems by difficulty to build metacognitive skills
Solve equations of the form: knownTotal + n × unknownWeight = totalWeight

designSystem.name: Singularity
designSystem.font: Poppins (300–800 weights, loaded via Google Fonts)

responsive.strategy: Container-query via ResizeObserver (not CSS media queries). The component measures its own container width and adapts all layout, typography, spacing, and SVG sizes dynamically.

adaptations.categorizeGrid: 3 columns → 2 on mobile; chip buttons flex-wrap on tiny screens
adaptations.solvePhase: Side-by-side (row) on desktop/tablet → stacked (column) on mobile with scroll overflow
adaptations.svgMobiles: Proportionally scaled item radius, font sizes, wire lengths per container size
adaptations.header: Shorter padding, smaller icon, abbreviated subtitle on mobile
adaptations.buttons: Check button shows '✓' instead of 'Check' on mobile; height/padding scaled
adaptations.scoreCard: flex-wrap on mobile, divider lines hidden on xs/sm
adaptations.animations: slideInUp replaces slideInLeft on mobile for stacked layout

parameters.description: The component uses width: 100% and aspect-ratio: 4/3 by default. Fixed width/height props are no longer needed — the tool auto-adapts to any container. These are kept for backwards compatibility but are optional.

width.description: Not typically needed. The container fills its parent width up to max-width 860px.

height.description: Not typically needed. Height is derived from aspect-ratio.

darkMode.description: Reserved for future dark mode support

additionalProps.description: Tool-specific dynamic content for hanging scale puzzles

puzzles.description: Array of puzzle data objects. Each puzzle represents a hanging mobile with known and unknown weights. Colors should use Singularity palette (#4A4DC9, #FF7212, #533086, #FC9145, #C1C1EA) for visual consistency.

totalWeight.description: Total weight displayed at the top of the mobile

branches.description: Array of branches hanging from the mobile bar

label.description: Emoji or text label for the item

weight.description: Weight of item. Use -1 for unknown items.

color.description: Color hex for item display. Use Singularity palette: #4A4DC9 (primary), #FF7212 (accent), #533086 (gradient start), #FC9145 (gradient end), #C1C1EA (light primary)

isUnknown.description: Whether this item's weight is unknown (to be solved). Unknown items show dashed orange (#FF7212) border with '= ?' label.

unknownLabel.description: Description of which items are unknown (shown to student in orange accent color)

answer.description: The correct weight of each unknown item

difficulty.description: Actual difficulty. Easy: orange-light bg (#FFF3E4). Medium: purple-light bg (#F3EEFF). Hard: red-light bg (#FDE8E8).

hint.description: Hint text shown in accent-light (#FFF3E4) card after first wrong attempt

showDifficultySort.description: Whether to show the categorization phase before solving

allowHints.description: Whether to allow hint display after wrong answer

maxAttempts.description: Maximum number of attempts per puzzle before moving on

defaultPuzzles.description: Uses built-in 6 puzzles (Fig 7.1-7.6) with Singularity colors. Fully responsive.

customEasySet.description: Custom 3 easy puzzles using Singularity palette colors

puzzles.hint: Apple weighs 3 and total is 10. So orange = 10 - 3

noCategorizationMode.description: Skip categorization and go straight to solving

categorize.description: Students see all 6 puzzles in a responsive grid (3-col desktop, 2-col mobile). Each puzzle shows a mini SVG mobile with animated swing. Students tap Easy/Medium/Hard chip buttons below each.
categorize.responsiveNotes: Grid collapses from 3 → 2 columns. SVG mobiles scale from 130px → 100px. Chip buttons flex-wrap on narrow screens.

solve.description: Students solve each puzzle sorted by their categorization. Shows an animated mobile SVG, question card with known/unknown counts, numeric input with pill-rounded Singularity styling, and instant feedback.
solve.responsiveNotes: Layout switches from side-by-side (row) to stacked (column) on mobile. SVG scales from 250px → 180px. Check button shows '✓' instead of 'Check' on mobile. Scrollable on mobile.

complete.description: Shows trophy animation, grade/score/solved stats in a flex-wrap card, per-puzzle results with difficulty chips, and 'Try Again' highlight button.
complete.responsiveNotes: Score card uses flex-wrap. Divider lines hidden on mobile. Font sizes scale down proportionally.

categorizePhase.description: Students tap Easy (🟢 green dot, #FFF3E4 bg) / Medium (🟡 amber dot, #F3EEFF bg) / Hard (🔴 red dot, #FDE8E8 bg) chip buttons below each mini-mobile.
categorizePhase.requiredAction: Categorize all puzzles before the 'Start Solving' button activates (switches from contained #4A4DC9 to highlight #FF7212).

solvePhase.description: Students type the numeric weight into a pill-rounded input (2px #C1C1EA border) and press the 'Check' contained button (#4A4DC9).

feedback.correct: Green gradient card with sg-popIn animation, auto-advances after 1.6s
feedback.wrong: Red gradient card with sg-shakeX animation, input shakes. Hint button (outlined #C1C1EA) appears after first wrong attempt.
feedback.maxAttemptsReached: Shows correct answer in red card, auto-advances after 1.8s

scoring.method: Points decrease with more attempts: (maxAttempts - attempts + 1) × 10
scoring.display: Star icon (#FF7212 fill) with score in accent-light chip (#FFF3E4 background, #B45309 text)

keyframes: sg-pulse — current puzzle dot in mini-map
sg-slideInLeft / sg-slideInRight — solve phase desktop panels
sg-slideInUp — solve phase mobile panels (replaces slideInLeft)
animations.swingAnimation: Continuous sinusoidal rotation (±2°) on mobile SVGs via requestAnimationFrame

teachingNotes.overview: Guide students through this interactive tool. Encourage exploration and discussion. The tool is fully responsive — works on classroom projectors, student tablets, and phones.
beforeStarting: Introduce the concept of hanging mobiles as a visual form of equations
Explain that the total weight at top equals sum of all hanging items
Remind students that unknown items (shown with dashed orange borders and '= ?') all have the SAME weight
On mobile devices, orient the phone in portrait mode for best experience
duringCategorization: Ask students why they think a puzzle is easy, medium, or hard
Discuss what makes a puzzle harder (more unknowns, more branches, larger numbers)
There are no 'wrong' categorizations — this builds metacognitive awareness
On tablets/phones, students can scroll down to see all puzzles in the 2-column grid
duringSolving: Encourage students to write the equation on paper: known + n×unknown = total
For wrong answers, have students explain their thinking before showing hints
Connect the mobile problems to formal algebraic equations (e.g., 3 + 2x = 16)
On mobile, the puzzle and input stack vertically — students can scroll between them
afterCompletion: Discuss which puzzles were hardest and why
Compare student categorizations with actual difficulty
Extend by asking students to create their own mobile puzzles
Use the 'Try Again' button to re-attempt with different categorizations

instructionsForStudent: Hanging mobile puzzles where the total weight is given and students must find the unknown weight at one branch. First, look at all 6 puzzles and decide if each is Easy, Medium, or Hard. Then solve them one by one — type the weight of each unknown item. You get 3 tries per puzzle and can ask for a hint after a wrong answer. Works on phones, tablets, and computers!
